intent: A folder grant is revoked mid-conversation and every later read fails closed while the chat and the folder data both survive.
steps: Attach a folder to Home chat through the native selection and trust flow and confirm the frontend holds only an opaque grant id and display metadata.
Ask a question the assistant can only answer by reading a file inside that folder and confirm the answer and its exact source manifest.
Revoke the grant from the folder chip.
Ask the same question again in the same conversation.
Ask the assistant to read the folder using the display name that still appears in an earlier compaction summary.
Move or replace the underlying folder on disk, re-grant it, and repeat the read.
Delete the chat and inspect the folder's own guarded store on disk.
expectedOutcome: A folder grant carries a grant id, display name, canonical identity digest, read access, trust revision, creation time, and an optional revocation time, and the canonical path stays Rust-private.
Every operation re-resolves the grant id, reopens the canonical root without following aliases, and rechecks trust, path containment, size, binary, hardlink, redaction, and capability limits.
After revocation the read fails closed with an ordinary-language explanation and an offer to choose the folder again, and the chat itself stays intact.
Moving or replacing the folder invalidates its canonical identity until the user approves it again, and the re-grant produces a fresh trust revision.
Revoking a grant leaves the chat and its historical accepted-source manifests readable as history.
Deleting the chat leaves the folder's data and any surviving grant untouched.
mustNotHappen: A revoked, missing, moved, or replaced grant never falls back to a permissive path; it always fails closed.
Compaction prose, a display name, or a model-authored reference never recreates, revives, or widens a grant.
A grant is never silently transferred to remote Browser content, to another conversation, or to a model-proposed path.
Deleting a chat never deletes folder data, folder memory, approval ledgers, or the folder's guarded store.
A read grant never confers writes, command execution, model startup, Browser actions, or arbitrary tool invocation.
The frontend never supplies a trusted filesystem root after grant creation.
